animation.notes: Verified on a Pixoo 64 (hardware 92), camera-timed, in two labs (2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05). FiestaBoard STREAMS on this device: every frame is its own single-frame Draw/SendHttpGif push (PicNum 1), which plays once with no overlay and no loop, and the last frame always lands cleanly. maxFps 5 is the measured stream rate: each push takes ~0.19 s whatever the frame size (64 px and 32 px alike); paced at 5 fps, 19 of 20 frames displayed (12 of 12 at 4 fps); back-to-back pushes reach ~4.2-5 fps with an occasional dropped middle frame; 6 fps cannot be sent. Two requests in flight drop frames, and Draw/CommandList shows only its last frame and is no faster, so frames go one at a time in order. Core-planned flip, slide, wipe, cascade, dissolve and fade, streamed at 5 fps, all displayed as intended (lab 2). Channel/SetBrightness answers in ~75 ms, so a fade through black (dim, swap, brighten) takes ~1.1 s. Why not an uploaded animation (lab 1): Draw/SendHttpGif uploads (one POST per frame, PicNum frames, PicOffset index, PicSpeed ms per frame, PicData base64 RGB888 row-major from the top left, PicWidth 64) LOOP FOREVER with no play-once flag; any upload longer than ~1.2 s (more than ~3 frames) shows a LOADING overlay; landing on a still after an animation keeps the old loop running with frame 0 replaced for ~5 s. PicID: a push displays only if PicID > the last accepted one (skipping ahead is fine); a reused or lower PicID still answers error_code 0 but is silently ignored. Draw/GetHttpGifId returns the next id (0 right after a reset). Draw/ResetHttpGifId does not clear the screen and needs no wait afterwards. Not verified: the community report of a freeze after ~300 pushes without a reset (the plugin resets every 32), and behaviour on other firmware. mDNS: the device advertises nothing.
sources: FiestaBoard hardware lab on a Pixoo 64, 2026-10-04 (camera-timed; fiestaboard-output--divoom-pixoo PR #1)
FiestaBoard hardware lab 2 on a Pixoo 64, 2026-10-05 (camera-timed single-frame streaming, brightness ramps, core-planned transitions)
